graphEvents.label: Failure modes across restarts, delivery, concurrency, injection and routines
Concurrent terminal and chat answers race on the item file
No prompt-injection boundary across memory, skills, chat and channels
Phase 002 has no missed-start misfire policy
Phase 010 has a lost-reply window between run and append
Reserved-id proposal items accumulate without bound
Phase 002 fatigue rule lacks failure definition and reset

label: Concurrent approvals from the terminal and a chat can silently discard the first answer: answerItem reads the item, checks state, then writes with no lock or compare-and-swap, so two callers that both read open both write and the last wins without item-answered-differently. The resume request is deduped by item id, but the recorded decision is not. Add a guarded write (lock file or write-if-unchanged on answer plus answeredAt) to phase 006's requirement and to 011 REQ-005, plus a concurrent-answer test.

No phase plan states a prompt-injection boundary: memory entries, skill bodies, chat transcripts and inbound channel messages all enter the same prompt as the bot body, and none of 005, 009, 010 or 011 says the block is untrusted, that the body and protocol outrank it, or that an instruction inside it is data. Add one shared requirement to all four phases and an injection fixture per phase.

Phase 002 defines no misfire policy for a routine start missed while the host slept or the agent restarted: starts[0] renders into the existing trigger and the matrix covers until outcomes and switch states, but nothing says whether a missed 09:00 cron is skipped or runs once on the next agent start. Add the policy to the routine requirement and one acceptance criterion.

Phase 010 has an unhandled lost-reply window: the conversation is append-only and a torn last line is skipped, but a crash after the run completes and before the bot message is appended leaves a human message with no reply and no marker, and nothing reconciles the conversation against run records. Add a recovery sentence to REQ-007 (report the gap on the next read, or a --repair verb that appends from the run record) or state the loss window and add a status cross-check.

Reserved-id proposal items can accumulate without bound: a memory-proposal holds no bot and awaits no resume, and skill proposals use the reserved skill-proposals id, so holdForBot never holds them and the ten-failure fatigue switch never sees them; a bot that emits [REMEMBER] every run adds one open item per run with no cap. Add a cap or expiry (for example 20 open proposal items per identity) to 005 REQ-007 and 009 REQ-005 with an acceptance criterion.

Phase 002's fatigue rule does not define failure or the reset: REQ-006 says ten consecutive failures disable the bot and bots enable restarts the count, but never says whether a refused run counts or whether a successful run resets the streak. Add both sentences to REQ-006 and mirror them in the acceptance criteria.

direction: Treating the approval index or the send queue as restart-fragile
reason: Both are file-backed and both have a stated restart test: the approval index is written before the send and resolves a press after a restart, and the queue writes an entry before the I/O and records an uncertain send unknown without retrying.

direction: Treating a re-sent chat message as a duplicate run
reason: Phase 010 uses the request event id as the human message id, and answerItem derives the resume request id from the item id, so the queue dedupes both.

direction: Treating holdForBot as a per-bot pile-up risk
reason: holdForBot returns the first open item for a bot and holds that bot while it is open, so real-bot items do not pile up; only reserved-id proposal items escape it.

question: Which phase owns the item-level lock or compare-and-swap that makes concurrent terminal and chat answers safe, and does the runtime already have a lock primitive the plan can reuse?
Does the runtime's posture and sandbox code already bound the damage a prompt injection can do, and is that bound enough to lower the injection finding from P1 to P2?
What is the misfire policy for a routine start missed while the host slept, and does the existing installer or launchd integration already define catch-up behavior the phase can cite?
Can memory-proposal and skill-proposal items accumulate without bound, and should a cap or expiry apply to reserved-id items?
